# A method on a user type that writes a top-level var compiles, and the write
# lands.
#
# Go has no receiver to hang one of these on -- the type is emitted into the
# same package as the Model -- so it is lifted to a free
# `CalcPending(k Calc)`. A package var is a field of that Model, and EvalIdent
# spells a state var `m.log` in every scope, so the lifted body named an `m`
# nothing in its signature declared: `undefined: m`.
#
# The Model arrives as a trailing parameter instead. One map decides both the
# signature and the argument, because a definition and a call site that each
# worked it out separately is the other half of what was wrong here.
#
# The two transitive legs are both present and neither touches a var of its
# own: `doubled` is a method reaching one through a method, `viaCalc` a
# top-level func reaching one through a method. Emitted without the Model,
# each would pass an argument the callee's signature has no room for.

sngl test --platform=bubbletea --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'PASS'
! stdout 'FAIL'

-- app.sngl --
import . "sngl:test"
import . "sngl:ui"

var log string = ""

struct Calc {
    base int
}

func Calc.pending(k Calc) int {
    log = log + "!"
    return k.base * 2
}

func Calc.doubled(k Calc) => k.pending() * 2

func viaCalc(k Calc) => k.doubled() + 1

component main node {
    var calc Calc = {base=3}
    var out = 0
    var note = ""

    effect(@mount {
        out = viaCalc(calc)
        note = log
    })

    text(value="{out}{note}")
}

func testTypeMethodWritesTopLevelVar(t Test, c main) {
    t.assert(c.out == 13)
    t.assert(c.note == "!")
}

window {
    main
}
